conviction_note: My four findings net to -0.5 points and they split across two lines that have gone opposite ways on this name before: the reported quarter reads modestly soft (consensus revenue sits at the 94th percentile of Thor's own unchanged FY26 guide) while the guide reads better than the tape implies (a 2026-09-10 centralisation of all North American RV operations with explicit cost-out language, and Thor's largest customer running the cleanest lot of the cycle). Against that I am adding roughly +1.5 points of positioning and taking the emitted number to +1.0: 9.6% of shares short with ~10 days to cover, put/call open interest 3.01, +4.62 vol points of put skew and a spot 2.6% off the 52-week low are all the same crowd already paid to be short, and the last two times this company lowered the bar at a guidance event the stock rose (2026-06-03, FY26 EPS guide cut ~12%, +2.86%; 2025-09-24, initial FY26 guide implying a 13-23% EPS decline off FY25's $4.85, +6.10%). +1.0 is deliberately far inside the 8.7% implied and inside the 5.56% median absolute reaction, because I have two real but offsetting document-backed reads and no directional edge large enough to justify more; the honest description of this name is a wide two-sided distribution with a small upward tilt from positioning.
bar: Q4 FY26 revenue $2.17-2.20bn and diluted EPS $0.91-0.97, two agreeing estimate sources (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/thor-industries-earnings-investors-brace-for-sharp-profit-decline-93CH-4909217 gives $0.91 on $2.17bn against $2.36 and $2.52bn a year ago; a second aggregation reported via https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/other/thor-industries-gears-up-for-q4-print-here-are-the-recent-forecast-changes-from-wall-streets-most-accurate-analysts/ar-AA2cfUbu gives $0.94-0.97 on $2.17-2.20bn), cross-checked against the company's own unchanged FY26 guide of $9.0-9.5bn net sales and $3.30-3.80 diluted EPS with nine-month actuals of $7.297bn and $2.59 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000730263/000073026326000019/thoq3fy26-earningsrelease.htm, 2026-06-03). I size -3.5% against the $2.17bn revenue bar.
positioning_check: 4,986,425 shares short at the 2026-08-31 FINRA settlement, 9.6% of shares, 9.96 days to cover on FINRA's reported average daily volume; Equibles models 5,091,730 as of 2026-09-15 with the official FINRA release due 2026-09-24, i.e. after the exit window (https://equibles.com/stocks/tho/short-interest, read 2026-09-21). I could not corroborate this from a second source - fintel.io returned HTTP 403 and capedge.com HTTP 404 to WebFetch - so it is single-source, but the sweep read the same file independently. The sealed baseline's skew is +4.62 vol points with put/call open interest 3.01 on 1,362 contracts and priced_direction_lean 'downside paid'. Conclusion: the short book, the skew and the option open interest all point the same way, the stock is 2.6% off its 52-week low and -42% from its high, and ~10 days to cover is a real squeeze mechanism. I have therefore cut both of my negative findings (Europe -2.5 to -2.0, revenue bar -1.5 to -1.0) and let the positioning carry the emitted number above the finding sum rather than filing positioning as a finding of its own.

findings.finding: German new-registration data published by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt shows Wohnmobile down 15.7% in July 2026 and down 21.4% in August 2026 - a two-month collapse in Erwin Hymer's home market against a January-July cumulative of only -3.3% - while Thor's European segment was still shipping +4.2% units and +11.8% net sales in the February-April quarter with backlog up just 1.0%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Europe is where this stock's last two large negative reactions originated: 2025-12-03 -9.48% and 2026-03-03 -5.56%, both quarters in which the FY26 EPS guide was under pressure. But the line has also gone the other way: on 2026-06-03 Thor cut the FY26 EPS guide from $3.75-4.25 to $3.30-3.80 and the stock rose 2.86%, and on 2025-09-24 it set an initial FY26 guide implying a 13-23% EPS decline and rose 6.10%. This is why the size is -2.0 and not larger.
findings.why_not_priced: The number is a single line item ('-21,4 %/1,9 %') inside a German-language KBA passenger-car press release published on 2026-09-03, eighteen days before this print. Every English-language THO preview I found anchors on RVIA wholesale and SSI retail, which are North American series; BMO's pre-print estimate cut was explicitly on 'softer retail and shipment trends' in the RV sector, i.e. the US data. The publicly circulating European datapoint is CIVD's seven-month figure of -3.0% overall and -3.3% for motor caravans, which is an order of magnitude milder than what July and August actually did, and CIVD's own Caravan Salon messaging in early September was that the industry 'expects recovery once the economic situation improves'. If the market had this, Thor's European segment - the leg that has grown net sales double digits for three straight quarters and carries ~38% of revenue - would be the thing preview notes name, and it is not. Net of the rest of the company (lesson 9): North America is ~62% of revenue and my read there is mildly positive, Thor Europe is taking share (24.4%, up), European backlog is +1.0% rather than falling, and the euro is roughly 3-4% stronger year on year (https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h10/hist/dat00_eu.htm), so the reported European quarter can still be up in dollars. That is why this is filed as a guidance finding about FY27 European wholesale and not as a reported-quarter finding, and why it is sized -2.0 rather than the -4.5 the retail number alone would suggest. Caveat I am carrying explicitly: KBA's 'Wohnmobile' is a Pkw sub-category and is narrower than CIVD's 'Reisemobile', so the two series are not identical in definition.
findings.independence: Knaus Tabbert, the listed German motorhome maker and Erwin Hymer's closest domestic competitor, reported H1 2026 revenue of EUR 503.9m, -11.9%, units -8.0%, and narrowed its FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin band to 5.0-6.0% citing 'weakened end-customer demand since spring' and 'continued cautious ordering behaviour from dealers' (https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/eqs-news-knaus-tabbert-veroeffentlicht-halbjahresfinanzbericht-2026-deutsch-543273.html, snippet_only - I read this from search output, not a successful fetch). Separately, a wave of German motorhome dealer and rental insolvencies through 2026 - Vanever/FreeVenture (7 August 2026), Schafhaeutle Reisemobile, HECK Caravan, amo caravaning, CMS Reisemobile - is documented at https://ms-aktuell.de/welt/vanever-insolvenz-wohnmobile-21-08-2026/ (2026-08-21, date confirmed in the URL path and in the body). These are different documents from the KBA release and point the same way.

findings.finding: Consensus Q4 revenue of $2.17-2.20bn requires Thor to print at or above the very top of its own unchanged FY26 guide: nine-month net sales are $7.297bn against a $9.0-9.5bn full-year range, so consensus sits at the 94th percentile of the guide while consensus EPS of $0.91-0.97 sits mid-range against the $0.71-1.21 the same guide implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Thor's reported-quarter surprises have not been what this stock trades on: on 2026-06-03 the quarter itself was weak (North American Towable net sales -24.6%, gross margin -470bp) and the stock still rose 2.86%. The two large down days, 2025-12-03 (-9.48%) and 2026-03-03 (-5.56%), both came with guidance pressure rather than with the printed quarter alone. That is the whole reason this finding is sized -1.0 against a -3.5% fundamental read.
findings.why_not_priced: This is arithmetic off two primary documents that nobody publishes in the preview: the guide and the nine-month actuals are in the Q3 8-K, the consensus is on the wire, and the join is not. If the market had done the join, the published revenue consensus would sit near $1.95bn (the guide midpoint) rather than $2.17bn, and the revenue line would be the one the previews flagged as at-risk rather than the EPS line. What stops me sizing this larger, and I am resolving rather than leaving the contradiction to be added by the sum (lesson 3): a bottom-up cross-check from RVIA monthly shipments over May-July 2026 (industry -14.7%, towables ~-15.3%, motorhomes ~-10.4%) applied to Q4 FY25 segment revenue of $888.7m / $557.4m / $923.1m lands at roughly $2.15bn, essentially at consensus, while backlog-conversion off the 30 April 2026 segment backlogs (-39.1% / -13.3% / +1.0%) lands at roughly $1.96bn, essentially at the guide midpoint. The two methods bracket $1.96-2.15bn, so my honest point estimate is about $2.09bn, ~3.5% below the bar - a real but small miss, and a miss that lands inside a range the company already guided to, which lesson 6 says is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect.
findings.independence: The FY25 Q4 segment revenue and the 31 July 2025 backlog used in the cross-check come from a different document, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/730263/000117184325006047/exh_991.htm (2025-09-24). The RVIA monthly shipment series is at https://www.rvnews.com/2026-rvia-wholesale-shipment-reports-2/ (May 22,900 -18.7%, June 25,484 -13.1%, July 19,948 -11.9%, motorhomes -25.6% in July). Note this finding shares the Q3 8-K with nothing else in this file - the backlog figures are used here only.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-10, twelve days before this print, Thor abandoned the decentralised operating model it has run for decades and put all North American RV operations under a single president and a single CFO, with the stated objective of 'drive out costs within the Company to strengthen our earnings profile' and benefits on an 'accelerated timeline' relative to the two-group structure announced earlier.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has paid for a self-help framing at a Q4 print before: on 2025-09-24, the equivalent event a year ago, Thor set an FY26 guide implying a 13-23% EPS decline off FY25's $4.85 and the stock rose 6.10%. The 2026-06-03 print, where management first put margin and cost language around a cut guide, went +2.86%. Both of the events on this line that carried a cost/structure narrative were bought.
findings.why_not_priced: The release was filed as a leadership-change announcement and the market read it as personnel: the stock is -5.38% over the five sessions to the seal and made a new leg toward its 52-week low after it. What the document actually contains is a structural reorganisation of a famously decentralised manufacturer with an explicit margin objective and no number attached, arriving twelve days before the one print of the year at which this company sets full-year guidance. If the market had priced it you would expect the pre-print drift to be positive rather than -5.38%, and you would expect at least one of the three pre-print analyst actions I could find (BofA target $96 to $86 on 2026-09-21, BMO estimate cuts, Wall Street Zen to Sell on 2026-09-20) to frame FY27 around a cost programme rather than around 'softer retail and shipment trends'. The inference I am making - that the FY27 guide arrives with a quantified structural-savings element - is an inference and not a disclosed number, which is why this is +1.5 and not larger.
findings.independence: The earlier two-group reorganisation is a separate release at https://ir.thorindustries.com/investor-resources/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/THOR-INDUSTRIES-ANNOUNCES-STRATEGIC-EVOLUTION-OF-NORTH-AMERICAN-OPERATING-MODEL-WITH-FORMATION-OF-TWO-RV-GROUPS/default.aspx (date not independently confirmed by me; the 2026-09-10 release references it as 'previously announced'). Corroborating, the Indiana Department of Workforce Development's current WARN list carries no 2026 notice from any Thor entity (https://www.in.gov/dwd/warn-notices/current-warn-notices/, read 2026-09-21) despite a 25% decline in towable unit shipments - Thor has been taking cost out through structure rather than through plant closures, which is consistent with the operating-model route and inconsistent with a capacity-cut route.

findings.finding: Camping World, Thor's largest customer and holder of record US new-unit share above 29%, exited its June 2026 quarter with new vehicles on the lot down ~17% year on year in units (dollars down only ~5%), prior-model-year exposure on new RVs near 1% against over 6% a year earlier, and units aged more than 365 days cut by over 60%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Thor's FY26 has been a story of the towable guide being cut on 'cautious independent dealer ordering patterns' (2026-06-03 release); the 2025-09-24 Q4 print noted the opposite - 'initiatives to gain market share began to deliver results' with towable wholesale -10.1% - and the stock rose 6.10%. A dealer-restock framing at a Q4 print has been bought on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, and I am sizing it accordingly at +1.0. This is a direct counterparty speaking after Thor last guided (lesson 5's standard), and it is the single largest offset to the 'channel is still stuffed' read that the RVIA-minus-SSI gap generates - US retail registrations ran -19.0% in May and -20.7% in June against wholesale of -18.7% and -13.1%, which looks like inventory building until you find that the largest single buyer's lot is 17% lighter in units with almost no carryover model years. The reason it is not fully in the price is that it is eight weeks old, sits in a competitor's transcript rather than in any THO preview, and cuts against the direction every RV headline since has taken. If the market had folded it in, the pre-print commentary would be about a 2027 restock rather than about 'softer retail and shipment trends'. Marked snippet_only: I read the inventory figures from search output of the Q2 2026 call, not from a successful fetch of the transcript.
findings.independence: The quarter itself is in the primary 8-K exhibit at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001669779/000110465926088141/cwh-20260729xex99d1.htm (2026-07-29), a different document from the transcript. Pointing the same way from a third party, Patrick Industries put dealer field inventory at roughly 18-20 weeks on hand against a pre-2020 norm of 26-30 weeks on its Q2 2026 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/30/patrick-industries-patk-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/, 2026-07-30). Pointing the other way, and I am netting it out rather than filing it separately: the same Patrick call cut its CY2026 RV wholesale forecast to 285,000-300,000 units, below RVIA's own Summer RoadSigns range of 300,000-328,100 (https://www.rvtrader.com/blog/2026/07/13/rvia-lowers-2026-rv-wholesale-shipment-forecast/).

outside_window.finding: FINRA's short-interest settlement for 2026-09-15 publishes on 2026-09-24, two sessions after the exit. Equibles models 5,091,730 shares short, +2.1% on the 2026-08-31 figure of 4,986,425 - shorts still building into the print - but the confirmation the market can trade on arrives after the window closes.

RVIA's August 2026 wholesale shipment report is not yet published as of 2026-09-21 - the RVIA reports page still shows July 2026 (19,948 units, 183,592 YTD) as the latest. It is the first read on Thor's FQ1 FY27 and on whether July's -25.6% motorhome print was an outlier, and it will land after this trade is closed.

The all-stock Patrick Industries / LCI Industries merger, targeting $150m of net annual run-rate cost savings, is expected to close in H1 2027. It consolidates two of Thor's three largest component suppliers into one counterparty and is a structural input cost question for FY27-28, not for this print.

searched_and_found_nothing: Indiana Department of Workforce Development current WARN notices for 2026: no notice from any Thor entity (Jayco, Keystone, Heartland, Cruiser RV, DRV, Airstream, KZ, Thor Motor Coach, Tiffin, Entegra, Dutchmen, CrossRoads, Highland Ridge) despite a 25% decline in towable unit shipments. The only 2026 Elkhart-county RV closure on the list is Forest River Plant 63, Bristol, 105 jobs, notice 2026-07-17, effective 2026-09-17 - Forest River is a Berkshire Hathaway company and not a Thor subsidiary, and at least one widely-shared September article implies otherwise (https://hoodline.com/2026/09/elkhart-county-rv-plant-closure-cuts-105-jobs-as-tariffs-squeeze-indiana-manufacturing/). No finding either way.

Insider activity: only three Form 4s in calendar 2026 (2026-01-16, 2026-03-09, 2026-06-17) and one Form 5 on 2026-09-02. No cluster, no pattern, nothing to size. https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000730263&type=4&dateb=&owner=only&count=20

IEEPA tariff refunds: the Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20 and the CIT has ordered roughly $165bn of refunds, but I could find no Thor-specific receivable, claim or accrual in the 30 April 2026 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000730263/000073026326000018/tho-20260430.htm) or in any 8-K, and Thor's Q3 commentary still describes tariffs as a live cost headwind rather than a recovery. Thor is mostly not the importer of record. Worth 0.

Thor 8-K flow since the last print: two filings, and the only substantive one is the routine $0.52 quarterly dividend declared 2026-06-16 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/730263/000073026326000021/tho-20260616.htm). No financing event, no covenant amendment, no buyback authorisation change to ask lesson 4's question about.

A dedicated company-level European disclosure for Erwin Hymer - registrations, order intake or dealer inventory - does not exist; CIVD's own market-data page carries only 2025 annual figures (https://www.civd.de/en/artikel/european-market/), which is why the KBA monthly series had to carry the European finding.
August 2026 RVIA wholesale shipments and the RVIA monthly seals report: not published or not publicly reachable as of 2026-09-21.
A second corroborating source for short interest: fintel.io returned HTTP 403 and capedge.com HTTP 404 to WebFetch.
baseline_tension: Mixed, and that is the honest answer: my one substantial negative (the German motorhome collapse in July-August) agrees with the +4.62 put skew, the 3.01 put/call open interest and the -12.53% twenty-day run-up, so to that extent I am inside the price - but my two positives (the 2026-09-10 operating-model centralisation and the cleanest dealer lot of the cycle at Thor's largest customer) cut against all three, and the 9.6% short interest with ~10 days to cover means the crowd paying for downside is exactly the crowd that gets run over if the FY27 guide is framed as trough-plus-self-help, which is what this management did at the last two guidance events.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (size a segment finding net of the rest) cut the German/KBA European finding from -2.5 to -2.0: Europe is ~38% of revenue, the other 62% is North America where my read is mildly positive, and within Europe Thor is gaining share (24.4%), backlog is +1.0% and the euro is ~3-4% stronger year on year, so the reported European quarter can still print up in dollars. I also moved it firmly to lands_on=guidance rather than reported_quarter for the same reason.

Lesson 5 (a narrow proxy loses to a broader series; macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until a company or direct counterparty says it) forced me to add the definitional caveat that KBA 'Wohnmobile' is narrower than CIVD 'Reisemobile', and to attach a direct competitor statement (Knaus Tabbert H1 2026: revenue -11.9%, 'cautious ordering behaviour from dealers') rather than let the government series stand alone. It did not kill the finding because the KBA months extend the CIVD series rather than contradicting it.

Lesson 3 (your own caveat has to reach the number, and resolve contradictions yourself) is what changed the revenue finding most: my RVIA bottom-up cross-check lands at ~$2.15bn, essentially at consensus, while backlog conversion lands at ~$1.96bn. Rather than leave a finding whose own text argues against it, I wrote the resolution into why_not_priced ($1.96-2.15bn bracket, ~$2.09bn point estimate) and cut the size from -1.5 to -1.0.

Lesson 7 (positioning is the thing to beat) cut both negatives and stopped me filing positioning as a fifth, positive finding. Crowded short plus paid-for downside is a reason to shrink a negative, not a separate long; it belongs in positioning_check and in the gap between the finding sum and expected_move_pct, where it now is.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar, keep findings inside the window) got me two agreeing estimate sources plus the company's own guide, so no small-size cap applies; it also moved the FINRA 2026-09-24 settlement, the August RVIA report and the PATK/LCII close out of findings and into outside_window at zero.

Lesson 2 / 'least priced is not most likely right' cut the operating-model finding from +2.0 to +1.5, because what the 2026-09-10 document establishes is the reorganisation, not a quantified saving - the FY27 savings number is my inference and the finding text now says so.
The 'asking what the market missed generates pessimism' note is why I kept both positives rather than dropping them for being less dramatic; it did not change a size.

Net effect on the sums: pre_lessons impact_sum -0.5, emitted impact_sum -0.5 - equal by coincidence, because the file cut my negatives by 1.0 point and my positives by 1.0 point. Four individual sizes all moved; expected_move_pct came down from +1.5 to +1.0 on lesson 1 and lesson 7 (the reaction function's veto and the crowded short both argue for a smaller absolute reaction than my fundamental read).
